colophon: Kaṇṇinuṇ Ciṟuttāmpu, graciously composed by Maturakavi Āḻvār.

lines.1: More than the great Māyan — who let himself be bound with a fine, slender rope —
lines.2: more than him, my own father,
lines.3: when I utter "Nampi of fair southern Kurukūr,"
lines.4: nectar sweeter than that wells up on my tongue.
lines.5: With my tongue I have found the joy of praising him again and again;
lines.6: I have truly attained his golden feet.
lines.7: I know no other god but Nampi of Kurukūr —
lines.8: I wander singing his sweet, melodious verses.
lines.9: Even as I wander about, I shall behold
lines.10: the dark, beautiful sacred form of the Lord of the gods —
lines.11: this is the good fortune I, this servant, have won:
lines.12: to belong, rightfully, to Nampi of the great, bountiful city of Kurukūr.
lines.13: Because the great scholars of the four Vedas
lines.14: would think it a lowly thing, to praise a mere man so —
lines.15: yet he rules me as both mother and father,
lines.16: such is the nature of my Nampi, Caṭakōpaṉ.
lines.17: Before, I placed my trust in the wealth of others,
lines.18: and I placed my trust in women —
lines.19: but today, become a loving devotee
lines.20: of Nampi of the red-gold-mansioned sacred Kurukūr, I have found true greatness.
lines.21: From today, and for all births to come, my Lord
lines.22: has graciously let me stand and praise his glory —
lines.23: Nampi of the mountain-mansioned sacred Kurukūr
lines.24: will never, ever scorn me — behold!
lines.25: Having seen and taken me in, the Lord Kārimāṟaṉ
lines.26: graciously stripped away my ancient, powerful karmas.
lines.27: I shall proclaim it, so that all eight directions may know,
lines.28: the grace of Caṭakōpaṉ of radiant Tamil.
lines.29: So that the devotees who celebrate his grace may rejoice,
lines.30: he graciously gave the meaning of that rare, hard-won Veda;
lines.31: by his grace he sang a thousand sweet Tamil verses —
lines.32: behold, his grace is the greatest thing in this world.
lines.33: He whom even the great scholars of the Veda hold
lines.34: as its inner meaning, sang it so it would endure, and set it firm in my heart —
lines.35: is this not the very fruit
lines.36: of the loving servitude I have entered, devoted to my worthy, glorious Nampi Caṭakōpaṉ?
lines.37: Even if it bears him no fruit, even if I am unfit,
lines.38: he corrects my ways and makes them good, and takes them as service to him —
lines.39: O Nampi of Kurukūr, ringed by groves loud with cuckoos,
lines.40: I strive only for love of your close-set, flower-crowned feet.
lines.41: He is loving to all who take refuge in him;
lines.42: he is loving toward Nampi of the southern city of Kurukūr —
lines.43: these are the very words spoken in love by Maturakavi;
lines.44: those who trust these words — behold, their home will be Vaikuṇṭham.
